library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: Liang F, Zhang Y, Xue Q, Zhang X. (2024). Integrated PBPK-EO
  modeling of osimertinib to predict plasma concentrations and intracranial
  EGFR engagement in patients with brain metastases. *Sci Rep* 14:12736.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-63743-z>
* PMC record (open access): <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11148161/>

This is a different paper from the same group's lung-tissue analysis,
`Liang_2024_osimertinib_qsp` (Front Pharmacol 2024, PMC10946252). The present
paper moves the target-engagement layer into brain tumour (BRT), changes the
equations and the rate constants, and adds two EGFR variants (wild type and
C797S). Hence the `2024b` year letter.

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Liang_2024b_osimertinib_qsp")
mod
```

# What is extracted, and what is not

| Layer | Content | Extracted? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Whole-body PBPK for osimertinib (PK-Sim 11.2; Rodgers-Rowland partitioning with a Kp scale of 1.5; six CYP intrinsic clearances; ABCB1 / BCRP efflux at the blood-brain barrier; Weibull dissolution) | **No** | A platform model. Its organ physiology, blood flows and permeability calculations are PK-Sim's internal defaults and are not printed. The deposited `.pksim5` project is a software artifact, and its binding block does not match Table 1 (see Assumptions). |
| 2 | EGFR occupancy (EO) in brain tumour for four EGFR variants, driven by the free osimertinib concentration in BRT | **Yes** | Eqs 3-5 are printed in full, and Table 1 gives every rate constant. |

The osimertinib concentration that drives layer 2 is supplied by the user
through the canonical time-varying covariate `CEFFECT`. In the paper this is
`C_OSI,BRT`, "the free OSI concentration in BRT", taken from the interstitial
sub-compartment of the PK-Sim brain. It is already unbound, so the model does
not multiply it by a fraction unbound.

# Population

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(mod)$population)
```

Liang 2024 is a simulation study. The virtual populations took race, dose,
subject numbers, age, proportion female, BMI and albumin from the clinical
studies in Table 2 (four plasma-PK and five intracranial-PK studies of NSCLC
patients, 4-49 patients each, aged 31-84 years). The dosing-regimen
simulations used 100 virtual patients with the demographics of Planchard et
al. (Japanese NSCLC, 75% female, median age 62.5 years). Population differences
act only in the PBPK layer; the EO parameters are shared by every scenario, so
population enters this model only through `CEFFECT`.

# Source trace

```{r source-trace, echo = FALSE}
tribble(
  ~Quantity, ~`Paper value`, ~`Model value`, ~`Source location`,
  "kon, wild type", "0.028", "0.028 x 60 = 1.68 /uM/h", "Table 1, 'kon EGFR (uM-1 s-1)' (kinact/Ki)",
  "kon, L858R + T790M", "1.40", "1.40 x 60 = 84 /uM/h", "Table 1",
  "kon, L858R", "0.57", "0.57 x 60 = 34.2 /uM/h", "Table 1",
  "kon, C797S", "0.0026", "0.0026 x 60 = 0.156 /uM/h", "Table 1",
  "koff", "0.001 /h", "0.001 /h", "Table 1; Methods text after Eq 5",
  "kdeg", "0.025 /h", "0.025 /h", "Table 1 (half-life 27.5 h)",
  "EGFR0 (EGFR T0)", "0.299 uM", "0.299 umol/L", "Table 1",
  "dEO/dt", "Eq 3", "d/dt(complex_*)", "Methods, Eq 3",
  "dEGFRfree/dt", "Eq 4", "d/dt(target_*)", "Methods, Eq 4",
  "EGFR occupancy (%)", "Eq 5", "ro_*", "Methods, Eq 5",
  "Driver C_OSI,BRT", "free conc. in BRT", "CEFFECT (umol/L)", "Methods, text after Eq 5"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Every equation and parameter, with its location in Liang 2024.")
```

The printed equations, with one free-EGFR / complex pair per variant:

```
(3)  dEO/dt       = kon * C_OSI,BRT * EGFRfree - koff * EO
(4)  dEGFRfree/dt = (EGFR0 - EGFRfree) * kdeg - kon * C_OSI,BRT * EGFRfree + koff * EO
(5)  EGFR occupancy (%) = (EGFR0 - EGFRfree) / EGFR0 * 100
```

## Units

Each ODE term must be in `umol/L per h`:

* `(rbase - target) * kdeg` = `umol/L * 1/h`. OK
* `kon * CEFFECT * target` = `1/(umol/L)/h * umol/L * umol/L`. OK
* `koff * complex` = `1/h * umol/L`. OK

The occupancy is a ratio of two `umol/L` quantities, reported as a percentage.
The only conversion in the file is `kon` x 60 (see Assumptions, item 1).

## Parameter table: paper against model file

```{r param-table}
ini_tbl <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf)[, c("name", "est", "fix")]
paper <- c(
  lkon_wt = log(0.028 * 60),
  lkon_l858r_t790m = log(1.40 * 60),
  lkon_l858r = log(0.57 * 60),
  lkon_c797s = log(0.0026 * 60),
  lkoff = log(0.001),
  lkdeg = log(0.025),
  lrbase = log(0.299)
)
ini_tbl |>
  mutate(
    `Back-transformed` = signif(exp(est), 4),
    Matches = ifelse(abs(est - paper[name]) < 1e-12, "yes", "NO")
  ) |>
  rename(Parameter = name, `File value (log)` = est, Fixed = fix) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Every ini() value against Table 1. All are fixed literature values.")

stopifnot(
  setequal(ini_tbl$name, names(paper)),
  all(abs(ini_tbl$est - paper[ini_tbl$name]) < 1e-12),
  all(ini_tbl$fix)
)
```

# Validation

The model is deterministic, has no dose and no residual error, so NCA does not
apply. The checks follow the mechanistic pattern: baseline hold, an exact
closed-form solution, and washout recovery. Each solve uses an observation
grid on the `target_wt` state; rxode2 returns every state and every `ro_*`
output at those rows.

```{r helpers}
variants <- c(
  ro_wt = "Wild type",
  ro_l858r_t790m = "L858R + T790M",
  ro_l858r = "L858R",
  ro_c797s = "C797S"
)

# Observation grid with a constant (or piecewise-constant) driver.
make_events <- function(times, ceffect) {
  data.frame(
    id = 1L,
    time = times,
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "target_wt",
    CEFFECT = ceffect
  )
}

solve_df <- function(model, events, ...) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = events, ...))
}

to_long <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    select(time, all_of(names(variants))) |>
    pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "occupancy") |>
    mutate(variant = factor(variants[output], levels = variants))
}
```

## 1. Baseline hold (zero exposure)

With no drug every free EGFR pool must stay at `EGFR0` and occupancy at 0.

```{r baseline}
sim0 <- solve_df(mod, make_events(seq(0, 336, by = 24), 0))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(sim0$target_wt - 0.299)) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(sim0$target_c797s - 0.299)) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(as.matrix(sim0[, names(variants)]))) < 1e-8
)
knitr::kable(head(sim0[, c("time", "target_wt", names(variants))], 3), digits = 6)
```

## 2. Exact solution at a constant concentration

At constant `C`, Eqs 3-4 are a linear system `x' = A x + b` in
`x = (EGFRfree, EO)` with

```
A = [ -(kdeg + kon*C)   koff ]      b = [ kdeg * EGFR0 ]
    [   kon*C          -koff ]          [ 0            ]
```

so `x(t) = x* + expm(A t) (x0 - x*)` with `x* = -A^-1 b`. The ODE solve must
match that closed form to integrator precision for every variant.

```{r closed-form}
closed_form <- function(kon, conc, times, koff = 0.001, kdeg = 0.025, r0 = 0.299) {
  A <- matrix(c(-(kdeg + kon * conc), kon * conc, koff, -koff), 2, 2)
  b <- c(kdeg * r0, 0)
  xstar <- -solve(A, b)
  e <- eigen(A)
  coef <- solve(e$vectors, c(r0, 0) - xstar)
  free <- vapply(times, function(t) {
    Re(xstar[1] + sum(e$vectors[1, ] * coef * exp(e$values * t)))
  }, numeric(1))
  (r0 - free) / r0 * 100
}

kon_h <- c(
  ro_wt = 0.028, ro_l858r_t790m = 1.40, ro_l858r = 0.57, ro_c797s = 0.0026
) * 60
conc_cf <- 0.0159
times_cf <- seq(0, 336, by = 2)
sim_cf <- solve_df(mod, make_events(times_cf, conc_cf), rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)

cf_err <- vapply(names(kon_h), function(o) {
  max(abs(sim_cf[[o]] - closed_form(kon_h[[o]], conc_cf, times_cf)))
}, numeric(1))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(variant = variants[names(cf_err)],
             max_abs_err_pct_points = formatC(cf_err, format = "e", digits = 2)),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Largest absolute difference (percentage points) between the ODE solve and the closed form, 0-336 h at 15.9 nmol/L."
)
# Measured about 1e-7 percentage points at these tolerances.
stopifnot(all(cf_err < 1e-4))
```

The closed form also gives the long-run behaviour of the printed system:
its fixed point is `EGFRfree = EGFR0`, so occupancy as defined by Eq 5 returns to
zero over a time scale of `1/koff` = 1000 h even under sustained exposure,
while the complex accumulates. Within the paper's 14-day horizon this decay is
small (a few percentage points for the two sensitive mutants).

## 3. Washout recovery

Stopping the drug after 14 days lets free EGFR re-synthesise at rate `kdeg`.
Because the printed Eq 3 gives the complex no degradation, the complex
accumulated during dosing (several times `EGFR0` after 14 days) keeps releasing
free EGFR at `koff * EO` after washout. Free EGFR therefore overshoots `EGFR0`
and settles near the quasi-steady value `EGFR0 + koff * EO / kdeg`, and the
Eq 5 occupancy turns negative. That is a property of the published equations,
and the check below confirms the model reproduces it.

```{r washout}
times_w <- seq(0, 672, by = 4)
sim_w <- solve_df(
  mod,
  make_events(times_w, ifelse(times_w < 336, 0.0159, 0)),
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
)
ro_end <- sim_w$ro_l858r_t790m[sim_w$time == 336]
ro_24h <- sim_w$ro_l858r_t790m[sim_w$time == 360]
last <- sim_w[sim_w$time == 672, ]
quasi_free <- 0.299 + 0.001 * last$complex_l858r_t790m / 0.025
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    quantity = c("complex at 336 h (umol/L)", "free EGFR at 672 h (umol/L)",
                 "EGFR0 + koff*EO/kdeg at 672 h (umol/L)", "occupancy at 672 h (%)"),
    value = c(sim_w$complex_l858r_t790m[sim_w$time == 336],
              last$target_l858r_t790m, quasi_free, last$ro_l858r_t790m)
  ),
  digits = 4, caption = "L858R + T790M pool after 14 days at 15.9 nmol/L and 14 days of washout."
)
stopifnot(
  ro_24h < ro_end,
  last$target_l858r_t790m > 0.299,
  # The complex drifts slowly (1/koff = 1000 h), so the quasi-steady value
  # holds to about 1%, not exactly.
  abs(last$target_l858r_t790m / quasi_free - 1) < 0.03
)
to_long(sim_w) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, occupancy, colour = variant)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 336, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "EGFR occupancy (%)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Constant 15.9 nmol/L for 14 days, then washout")
```

# Replication of Figure 2B: four EGFR variants over 14 days

Figure 2B shows occupancy in BRT for the four variants over 14 days of 80 mg
once daily. Its driver is the PBPK model's free BRT concentration, which is not
reproducible here. Liang 2024 Table 3 brackets that concentration at steady
state: predicted intracranial Ctrough 10.3-15.9 nmol/L and Cmax 12.7-20.2
nmol/L across the five brain-metastasis studies. The model is therefore run at
constant concentrations spanning that range: 10.3 nmol/L (lowest predicted
trough) and 20.2 nmol/L (highest predicted peak).

```{r fig2b}
times_b <- seq(0, 336, by = 2)
brackets <- c(`10.3 nmol/L` = 0.0103, `20.2 nmol/L` = 0.0202)
sim_b <- bind_rows(lapply(names(brackets), function(nm) {
  to_long(solve_df(mod, make_events(times_b, brackets[[nm]]))) |>
    mutate(driver = nm)
}))

ggplot(sim_b, aes(time, occupancy, colour = variant)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = 3, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~driver) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "EGFR occupancy (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2B of Liang 2024 (driver held constant; see text).")
```

```{r fig2b-table}
# Day-14 values read off Figure 2B by the maintainers (trough to peak of the
# last dosing interval). The Results text gives "approximately 10%" for C797S
# and above 80% for L858R + T790M and L858R.
fig2b <- tibble(
  variant = factor(variants, levels = variants),
  `Figure 2B, day 14 (%)` = c("46-49", "88-92", "85-89", "8-9")
)
day14 <- sim_b |>
  filter(time == 336) |>
  select(variant, driver, occupancy) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = driver, values_from = occupancy)

day14 |>
  left_join(fig2b, by = "variant") |>
  rename(Variant = variant,
         `Model, 10.3 nmol/L (%)` = `10.3 nmol/L`,
         `Model, 20.2 nmol/L (%)` = `20.2 nmol/L`) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Occupancy at 336 h.")

lo <- setNames(day14$`10.3 nmol/L`, as.character(day14$variant))
hi <- setNames(day14$`20.2 nmol/L`, as.character(day14$variant))
stopifnot(
  # Paper's efficacy statement: both sensitive mutants above 80% in BRT.
  lo[["L858R + T790M"]] > 80, lo[["L858R"]] > 80,
  # Paper's resistance statement: C797S about 10%.
  hi[["C797S"]] < 15,
  # Rank order of Figure 2B.
  all(lo[["L858R + T790M"]] > lo[["L858R"]], lo[["L858R"]] > lo[["Wild type"]],
      lo[["Wild type"]] > lo[["C797S"]])
)
```

The day-14 occupancies agree with Figure 2B semi-quantitatively: the two
sensitive mutants sit above the 80% efficacy line (the model is 2-10 points
higher), wild type sits at 34-50% against about 48%, and C797S at 5-9% against
about 8-10%. What the constant driver cannot reproduce is the slow climb over
the first week in Figure 2B. That climb follows the accumulation of the PBPK
brain concentration towards steady state, which is a property of layer 1.

## The printed kon unit

The same simulation with `kon` taken literally as `uM^-1 s^-1` (x3600 into
hours) shows why the model file reads the Table 1 values as per minute:

```{r printed-unit}
mod_printed <- mod |>
  rxode2::ini(
    lkon_wt = log(0.028 * 3600),
    lkon_l858r_t790m = log(1.40 * 3600),
    lkon_l858r = log(0.57 * 3600),
    lkon_c797s = log(0.0026 * 3600)
  )
sim_p <- bind_rows(lapply(names(brackets), function(nm) {
  to_long(solve_df(mod_printed, make_events(times_b, brackets[[nm]]))) |>
    mutate(driver = nm)
}))
day14_p <- sim_p |>
  filter(time == 336) |>
  select(variant, driver, occupancy) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = driver, values_from = occupancy)
day14_p |>
  left_join(fig2b, by = "variant") |>
  rename(Variant = variant,
         `Printed unit, 10.3 nmol/L (%)` = `10.3 nmol/L`,
         `Printed unit, 20.2 nmol/L (%)` = `20.2 nmol/L`) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Occupancy at 336 h with kon read as printed (per second).")

c797s_printed <- day14_p$`10.3 nmol/L`[day14_p$variant == "C797S"]
stopifnot(c797s_printed > 50)
```

Read per second, C797S occupancy at the paper's own lowest intracranial
concentration is about `r round(c797s_printed)`%, and wild type is near
saturation. That reverses the paper's central conclusion that low C797S
occupancy explains on-target resistance, and contradicts Figure 2B.

# Figure 2A: the in-vitro comparison

Figure 2A compares the model with T790M/L858R inhibition measured in NCI
cells at 100 nmol/L, where the observed inhibition sits at about 80-84% over
24 h and the paper's simulated curve peaks near 82%. A constant 100 nmol/L
driver in this model gives near-complete occupancy of the double mutant within
hours:

```{r fig2a}
sim_a <- solve_df(mod, make_events(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), 0.1))
to_long(sim_a) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, occupancy, colour = variant)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "EGFR occupancy (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Constant 100 nmol/L; compare Figure 2A of Liang 2024.")
knitr::kable(sim_a[sim_a$time %in% c(6, 24), c("time", names(variants))], digits = 1)
```

Figure 2A is not reproduced under either `kon` reading. The curve the paper
shows there is driven by a PK profile (dotted line, peak about 115 nmol/L) and
by binding inside the PBPK model, where target-mediated depletion and the
intracellular sub-compartment both act; the panel caption does not say which
concentration drove it. This is recorded as a limitation, not adjusted for.

# Assumptions and deviations

1. **`kon` is read as `uM^-1 min^-1`, not the printed `uM^-1 s^-1`.** This is
   an inferred unit correction, chosen by the maintainers because the printed
   unit makes the model contradict the paper's own Figure 2B and its C797S
   conclusion (see the section above), while the per-minute reading reproduces
   both. Per-minute is PK-Sim's base unit for a second-order rate constant, so
   values entered in base units and labelled per second in the table is a
   plausible mechanism. Supplementary Table S3 also supports a near-saturated
   double mutant: the sensitivity coefficient of EO trough to `kon` is only
   -0.1 / 0.07. The numeric values are Table 1's; only the time unit changed.
   To recover the literal reading, multiply each `kon` by 60, as in the
   `mod_printed` chunk.

2. **The deposited PK-Sim project was not used as a parameter source.** The
   `.pksim5` file (supplement 1) holds a single binding process whose constants
   differ from Table 1 on every value (`koff` 0.001 per minute rather than per
   hour; `Kd` 0.12 nmol/L, implying `kon` = 8.33 uM^-1 min^-1; target half-life
   0.6 min rather than 27.5 h). Table 1 is the published statement of the model
   and is what is encoded.

3. **The PBPK layer is not extracted;** `CEFFECT` stands in for it. Two
   consequences follow. (a) With an external driver, occupancy is independent
   of `EGFR0` (Eqs 3-5 are linear in the EGFR states), so Figure 3G-H, where a
   higher EGFR T0 lowers occupancy, cannot be reproduced; that effect comes
   from target-mediated depletion of drug inside the PBPK. (b) Figure 2A and
   the first-week shape of Figure 2B depend on the PBPK driver.

4. **The driver is the interstitial free concentration.** The Methods state
   that `C_OSI,BRT` is the free concentration in the interstitial
   sub-compartment of the brain; Supplementary Figure S1 says the occupancy is
   simulated "within the intracellular compartment". The model follows the
   Methods. Either way the user supplies the concentration.

5. **Eqs 3-5 are encoded as printed.** The complex has no degradation term, so
   total EGFR rises above `EGFR0` under exposure (to about nine times
   `EGFR0` after 14 days at 15.9 nmol/L for the double mutant), the Eq 5
   occupancy (depletion of free EGFR relative to baseline) relaxes to zero
   over about `1/koff` = 1000 h of sustained exposure, and after washout free
   EGFR overshoots `EGFR0` so the occupancy turns negative (Validation,
   section 3). This is the published structure and was not changed; it
   matters only for simulations much longer than the paper's 14 days or that
   stop dosing.

6. **Wild type and C797S are separate single-variant pools.** The paper
   labels the fourth variant "C797S" without giving its background (clinically
   it arises on L858R/T790M); it is encoded as its own pool with the Table 1
   `kon`.

7. **No IIV and no residual error are encoded.** Liang 2024 generated
   variability by sampling PK-Sim virtual populations in the PBPK layer and
   fitted no random effects on the EO layer.

8. **Constant-concentration validation.** The Figure 2B comparison holds the
   driver constant at the Table 3 bounds rather than reconstructing a daily
   profile, because the within-day brain concentration profile is not
   published.
